summary: Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He earned a master's degree at the University of Auckland (~1999–2001) and a Ph.D. under Hildegard Diemberger at the University of Cambridge (~2007–2011). He held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology, Columbia International University Korntal (~2006–2019), and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (2019).

Adrián Muñoz works in Indology and religious studies. His career includes appointments as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and as lecturer of South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and has held posts at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008 and 2026).

Agathe Keller is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She has held affiliations with REHSEIS (attested 2006), the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2017), and Paris Diderot University (attested 2017).

Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Akademisches Gymnasium and the University of Vienna (~1946–1948). He taught at Delhi, Banaras Hindu, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, Tokyo, and Kyoto, before serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw (~1996–2001) and earned a PhD from Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~2002–2007). She held posts at Cornell University (attested 2009) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (1873, 1880–1888), receiving the Geshe Lharampa degree. He taught the 13th Dalai Lama and Geshe Wangyal, and founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and Atsagat Datsan (1913).

Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Anant Sadashiv Altekar, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at the University of London under K. de B. Codrington. He held major posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam University.
Aiko Okoshi worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1970–1975) and became a lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College (~1974–1977) and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010), which he founded in 1996, and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.

Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1969–1972) and under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah (1974). He has served as abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery since ~1995.
Ajahn Khemadhammo is active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Drama Centre London (~1963–1966) and trained under the traditional teacher Ajahn Chah (~1972–1977).

Ajahn Pasanno is a Buddhist studies practitioner who studied under the traditional teacher Ajahn Chah (~1974–1982). He served as the founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from ~1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971) and trained under Ajahn Sumedho starting in 1977. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at the University of Washington and UC Berkeley, and trained under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977). He founded and was abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and was abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and served as a Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
Akhil Rajeev P is a researcher in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao (1979–2002). He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1998), Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, Kyoto Women's University (attested 2009), and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy (attested 2009).

Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and earned his PhD at the University of Paris / Sorbonne Nouvelle (~1980–1983). He held posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, where he served as professor and vice president.

Akihiro Oda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Otani University. He has served as a full-time lecturer (attested 1992) and as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) at Otani University.
